    **The eternal knower: "I was never not"** Memory seems to bind the self to the past — to what the self has itself experienced. But then the objection arises, and it is a sharp one. "I was not at the time of the Rāmāyaṇa," the reader says. "Vālmīki composed it long ago, and I was not there to experience it; so how can the self, which remembers only what it has experienced, be the eternal knower?"
